newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says oil refining capacity at 1.24 mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: Iran says oil refining capacity at 1.24 mln bpd.

text.p: Iran's oil refining capacity is 1.24 million barrels per day (bpd), but actual runs can reach 17 percent above this, an Iranian oil official said on Sunday.

"Just now, potentially, we can increase our capacity 17 percent more than this figure (1.24 million bpd) because during the (1980-1988) war (with Iraq) we had modifications and projects to increase capacity," said Sayyed Reza Kasaeizadeh, director of refining affairs at the National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company (NIORDC).

Refining capacity at the country's eight refineries was: Abadan 400,000 bpd, Isfahan 265,000 bpd, Tehran 225,000, Arak 150,000 bpd, Tabriz 110,000 bpd, Shiraz 40,000 bpd, Kermanshah 30,000 bpd and Lavan 20,000 bpd.
Product exports, mainly fuel oil and naphtha, ran close to 200,000 bpd. Domestic demand for petroleum products was growing at an annual rate of three to four percent, Kasaeizadeh said.
Refinery run-rates above nominal capacity were usually achieved just prior and during the winter months when local demand for heating and other fuels increased.
Iranian kerosene and gas oil demand usually reached 85 million litres a day in the winter, compared to below 80 million litres the rest of the year, Kasaeizadeh said.
Additional refining capacity will come on stream when commissioning begins at the 232,000 bpd Bandar Abbas plant.
"Construction is going to probably finish in March, commissioning of a crude unit in April," he said.
Hydrocracking and hydrogen units would go into operation some six months after commissioning, he added.
Bandar Abbas would supply seven million litres a day of unleaded gasoline for the domestic market where it would be blended with regular gasoline to reduce overall lead levels.
Iran is set to become self-sufficient in oil products once the Bandar Abbas refinery goes onstream, Kasaeizadeh said.
"From March there will be no product imports," he said, but did not give a figure for current imports.
Oil traders still expect Iran to import gasoline or heating oil cargo during harsh winters.

National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) will also continue to rely on a processing deal in Italy and a provision that allows it to export some 150,000 bpd of crude in exchange for products to ensure a completely balanced product distribution.

"Iran is now approaching self-sufficiency in petroleum products...Once the Bandar Abbas refinery is operational...Iran will be truly self-sufficient since that will substantially boost its output of middle distillates," according to the Arab Oil and Gas Journal.
Future downstream projects included a condensate refinery at Bandar Abbas but the emphasis in downstream policy was to upgrade rather than expand capacity.
"We are intending to substitute natural gas in place of many oil products. Hence, we need not to increase oil refining capacity but upgrade the qualities," Kasaeizadeh said.
This would centre on units for kerosene desulphurisation, catalytic reforming unit for gasoline with continuous regeneration and isomerization units to produce unleaded gasoline, he said.
